1. FIELD SHAPE AND NAME. `ProjectionDelta.vector_unsupported_kinds: Vec<String>` (engine + pyo3 + Python SDK); `vectorUnsupportedKinds: string[]` (napi + TS SDK). It is a list of node KINDS, sorted and de-duplicated (SELECT DISTINCT ... ORDER BY kind), EMPTY rather than absent, OUTPUT-ONLY. Named for the AXIS: the three sibling vectors are projection ATTRIBUTE NAMES, this one is node KINDS, so the name says `kinds` out loud; the `vector_` prefix binds it to the dense arm because a reported kind is still fully FTS/lexically searchable (without it the field reads as 'kinds FathomDB does not support', which is false and alarming); 'unsupported' rather than 'skipped'/'failed' because nothing was retried and nothing errored. Kept a Vec<String> rather than a Vec<{kind, reason}> struct: there is exactly ONE reason a kind can appear, so a reason field would be a single-variant enum, and a struct would mean a net-new #[napi(object)] plus a net-new #[pyclass] on the slice you flagged as most likely to add surface. Both SDK suites assert the negative in both directions (no attribute name in the report, no kind in `deferred`) so the two axes cannot later be merged silently.

2. READINESS SEMANTICS ARE UNCHANGED — confirmed, and pinned by a dedicated test in each language: Rust `readiness_semantics_are_unchanged_by_the_report` (tests/tc67_unsupported_vector_kind_report.rs), Python `test_readiness_semantics_are_unchanged_by_the_report`, TS `readiness semantics are unchanged by the report`. Deliberately separated from the report test and built on the harshest fixture — a corpus of ONLY unsupported kinds with the dense arm declared — because the tempting 'fix' (treat an unsupported kind as unfinished work) would satisfy a report-only assertion while wedging every consumer whose corpus contains one. It asserts dense_readiness == Ready and that drain returns, then writes MORE unsupported rows and re-asserts. slice20_dense_readiness (8/8) and slice20c_flush_barrier (12/12) are also green.

3. DECLARE-TIME RESIDUAL — I took OPTION (a): the report is computed at declare time from the kinds already in canonical_nodes, so a non-committable kind written LATER is absent from a delta the caller already holds; the documented refresh is to re-apply the same spec, an idempotent no-op that returns a current report (which works only because the report is state-keyed, not diff-keyed, and does not feed `unchanged`). Option (b) was rejected because read_projections returns Vec<ProjectionSpec> and ProjectionSpec is the CALLER-AUTHORED declaration type: hanging the report there would need either a second accept-inert field (the dense_readiness treatment) on a type whose whole contract is 'what you declared', or a change to read_projections' return type — both larger and more governed than the fact warrants. Documented in the design note §5, in all three dev/interfaces docs, and in CHANGELOG.
